_doc: Registry of /data map layers. Served via /api/data/layers. Every layer is labeled kind: 'raw' (as-is display, source attribution, no predictive claim) or 'signal' (interpreted reading; may not surface before ROOT VALIDATION LADDER gate 2). Status: live | awaiting_key | planned. Layers with field:true are visual FIELD overlays and inherit registry-native display controls (opacity slider, default 60%). group: panel section id (BUILD ORDER 4 #2, GIP Part 4 UI SCALABILITY) — the client's PANEL_GROUPS/LAYER_GROUP map is now a fallback only; a new layer can be slotted into an existing panel group by setting this field alone, no client code change required (a brand-new group id needs one addition to client PANEL_GROUPS to get a label, but defaults collapsed automatically). costTier: 'light'|'moderate'|'heavy' — relative client network/render cost (raster fields and high-frequency live streams are 'heavy'; small polled REST lists are 'light'); feeds the panel's active-cost-budget advisory badge (client datamap.tsx costWeightOf/activeCostWeight) and is available for future admission-control budgets as the registry grows toward hundreds of layers. REGISTRY v2 (EARTH TWIN A2, 2026-07-15 — all fields OPTIONAL and additive; server/layersRegistry.test.ts is the machine-checked contract): altitudeRef = what z means for the layer (surface|agl|msl|orbit|depth|underground). time = what the global time axis can do with the layer ({mode: live|dated-daily|dated-subdaily|archive|static, latencyDays?, historyStart? — the honest archive floor, YYYY-MM}). lod = camera-altitude visibility envelope in km for the LOD director ({camMinKm?, camMaxKm?, fadeBandKm?, ramp?}) — LOD is a render choice, always reversible by zoom, never a storage choice, and an out-of-envelope layer states so on-panel (never a silent drop). provenance = {license?, commercialOk?, updateFreq?, resolution?, coverage?, confidence: verified|derived|estimated|inferred|placeholder} — commercialOk:false may NEVER ship (license ratchet: the monetization tripwire made machine-checkable; use build-first alternatives or a paid-license wishlist entry). renderKind = which generic engine draws the layer (point-symbol|raster-field|vector|track|grid|custom).

layers.name: Satellite imagery
layers.source: Esri World Imagery (tiles; attribution on-map)
layers.description: Base satellite/aerial imagery.

layers.name: Terrain (3D relief)
layers.source: Mapterhorn terrain tiles (Copernicus GLO-30 + national open DEMs; © Mapterhorn)
layers.description: Real 3D elevation relief: the globe mesh is deformed from the DEM so mountains rise and valleys sink (best with pitch/tilt), plus a hillshade accent under all data layers. Off by default — opt-in premium relief; global elevation from Copernicus GLO-30 + national open DEMs. VERTICAL EXAGGERATION — multiplies terrain height so mountains and valleys read clearly from altitude. Elevation data stays real; only the look changes. 1.0× — true scale (Earth looks nearly flat) · 1.3× — balanced · default · 3.0× — dramatic relief.

provenance.license: Copernicus GLO-30 + national open DEMs; © Mapterhorn tiles (commercial-OK per licensing register 2026-07-04)

layers.name: Seafloor (drain the ocean)
layers.source: GEBCO_2024 shaded relief via GEBCO WMS (BODC), 15 arc-sec; depth tint + 3D basin mesh from NOAA ETOPO1 via Terrain Tiles on AWS (Mapzen/Tilezen, open data); NOAA ETOPO 2022 hillshade as automatic fallback; native-resolution GEBCO_2026 15 arc-sec depth grid self-tiled per region (see seafloor_confidence's committed regions) blended on top where available
layers.description: Ocean-floor relief: toggling drains the ocean — GEBCO_2024 shaded relief (mid-ocean ridges, trenches, fracture zones) under a depth tint, and with 3D terrain on the basins physically sink (the globe mesh deforms below sea level). HONESTY: soundings + satellite-gravity interpolation — only ~a quarter of the world's seafloor is direct-measured, so depths are indicative, never navigational; while drained, LAND shows GEBCO's hypsometric tint instead of satellite imagery (a raster cannot be elevation-masked). Per-cell measured-vs-interpolated (TID) confidence ships as its own toggleable overlay, seafloor_confidence. Inside that layer's committed regions (Mariana Trench today), this layer additionally blends in the SAME native-15-arc-sec GEBCO_2026 grid the confidence overlay was built from — same depth palette, sharper relief — and falls back to the global ~1 arc-min ETOPO1 tint everywhere else; regions grow by pipeline run, no code change (research/earth_twin_program.md).

provenance.license: GEBCO Grid: public domain, commercial use allowed, attribution requested (doi:10.5285/1c44ce99-0a0d-5f4f-e063-7086abc0ea0f); Terrain Tiles: open (Mapzen / AWS Open Data); NOAA ETOPO: US-gov public domain
provenance.resolution: 15 arc-sec (GEBCO_2024 relief, native to z8; GEBCO_2026 depth blend inside committed regions); mesh/tint ~1 arc-min (ETOPO1) elsewhere

layers.name: Seafloor mapping confidence
layers.source: GEBCO_2026 TID grid (GEBCO Bathymetric Compilation Group; public domain, attribution required)
layers.description: Measured-vs-predicted seafloor: every cell colored by GEBCO's own documented source type — direct measurements (echo-sounders, lidar, seismic, soundings) vs indirect (satellite-gravity prediction, algorithmic interpolation) vs unknown provenance. The Earth Twin charter's uncertainty display, verbatim from the source: where seafloor mapping is partial we SAY so (the shipped Mariana demo region measures 65.9% direct / 34.1% predicted — computed from the data, never quoted). Data + pipeline (scripts/gebco_seafloor_tiles.py -> seafloor_tid_mariana.pmtiles; decode table datacore/gebco/tid_decode.json; client lib client/src/lib/seafloorV2.ts) + datamap wiring shipped. Coverage honesty: regional demo (Mariana Trench, 138-146E / 7-15N) — never presented as global; the pipeline scales region by region, and the map renders nothing (not a guessed class) outside a committed region's bbox.

provenance.license: GEBCO Grid: public domain; commercial use explicitly allowed; attribution required; NOT for navigation (terms fetched 2026-07-16)
provenance.coverage: demo region: Mariana Trench (138-146E, 7-15N); regional subsets by pipeline run

layers.name: Day/Night & Moon
layers.source: Computed ephemeris (Meeus low-precision solar/lunar series) — pure computation, no external feed
layers.description: The live day/night terminator shading the night side of the globe, with the subsolar point (where the sun is directly overhead right now) and the sublunar point (where the moon is overhead) carrying its real phase. HONESTY: display-grade ephemeris — subsolar good to ~0.01°, sublunar to ~1° (truncated lunar series); shading clamps at ±85° latitude (web-mercator limit). Computed, labeled as such — never presented as survey ephemeris.

layers.name: Weather radar (US)
layers.source: NOAA/NWS nowCOAST WMS (public domain)
layers.description: US base-reflectivity radar mosaic, refreshed ~5 min, rendered under all data layers. COVERAGE HONESTY: US + territories only — no free lawful global radar source exists (RainViewer and Open-Meteo free tiers prohibit our use). Global temp/wind fields can activate later via an OpenWeatherMap free key (human action filed).

layers.name: Temperature (global)
layers.source: OpenWeatherMap free tier (Weather data © OpenWeatherMap; attribution required)
layers.description: Global surface-temperature field, model-derived (not station truth — labeled per the licensing register). Tiles proxied server-side so the API key is never exposed and the 60-calls/min free budget is shared-cache bounded. Fresh keys take ~2h to activate on OWM's side — the layer shows a retry note, not an error, until then.

layers.name: Wind (global)
layers.source: OpenWeatherMap free tier (Weather data © OpenWeatherMap; attribution required)
layers.description: Global wind-speed field, model-derived (not station truth). Same proxied-key + shared-cache + fresh-key-retry behavior as the temperature layer.

layers.name: Live aircraft (ADS-B)
layers.source: adsb.lol (ODbL 1.0; primary) + airplanes.live + adsb.fi (fallbacks)
layers.description: Live aircraft positions; updates ~10s. Icon → 3D ramp (EARTH TWIN E3): class icons at wide zooms; at close zoom (z8+) aircraft render as heading-oriented 3D silhouettes at their REAL barometric altitude — with tilt and 3D terrain on, planes fly above the ground (altitude scaled with the terrain's own exaggeration so the vertical datum matches). Color = altitude band in both representations (ground grey / <3,000 m amber / cruise blue). On-ground aircraft sit at the surface; negative baro readings clamp to 0, never below it. No predictive claim.

provenance.license: adsb.lol ODbL 1.0 (the monetization-lawful provider per the wishlist compliance check)
provenance.coverage: community receiver network — coverage varies by region

layers.name: Satellites (live)
layers.source: CelesTrak GP element sets (T.S. Kelso; client-fetched in the browser, SGP4 propagated on-device)
layers.description: Live positions of the tracked near-earth satellite population (~8,000+ of the ~16,000 catalogued objects), propagated on-device from CelesTrak GP elements with SGP4 and drawn as GPU points colored by orbit class (LEO/MEO/GEO). REAL positions only: deep-space objects (most GEO comms and MEO navigation sats) require SDP4, which the near-earth kernel does not implement — they are skipped and COUNTED in the layer status, never fabricated. No predictive claim.

layers.name: US power plants
layers.source: Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0 (WRI, CC BY 4.0)
layers.description: All ~9,800 US plants by fuel type; capacity + operator on click. Static reference data (2021 vintage).

layers.name: EPA CAMD plant operations (ground truth, TX pilot)
layers.source: U.S. EPA Clean Air Markets Division (CAMD) Continuous Emissions Monitoring, unit-level daily (public domain, 40 CFR Part 75)
layers.description: Direct plant-utilization ground truth from EPA's own unit-level Continuous Emissions Monitoring reporting — the ladder gate-1 truth source for the power vertical's satellite/imagery inference roots, not itself a trading signal. v1 pilot scope: Texas only (matches GRID VISION's ERCOT focus); quarterly cadence — a quarter is only queryable once fully closed, so this is NOT live/daily despite per-day granularity inside each record. Marker color is a DATA-DRIVEN utilization tier (operating hours actually reported, as a fraction of every possible unit-hour that quarter) — not fuel type; facilities whose EPA facility/attributes join missed a position are honestly omitted, never guessed. Served via the shared api.data.gov DEMO_KEY unless a dedicated EPA_CAMD_API_KEY is configured (disclosed on click).

layers.name: US nuclear reactor status (NRC, daily)
layers.source: U.S. NRC daily Power Reactor Status Reports (nrc.gov, public domain, keyless)
layers.description: Percent-of-rated-thermal-power reported daily by the NRC for every operating US commercial reactor, joined onto the WRI/HIFLD nuclear-plant registry's coordinates (server/nrcReactorStatus.ts's joinToPlants — an NRC unit that can't be resolved to a registry plant is dropped, never guessed at a nearby site). Marker color is a DATA-DRIVEN status tier off today's mean reported power across a plant's units (full / reduced / outage / unknown-no-reading) — not fuel type, and distinct from the static powerplants/HIFLD layers' capacity snapshot. NRC collects this once daily (4am-8am ET); not a live/real-time feed. GATE 1 (DATA) passed 2026-08-04 (datacore/signal_ladder.json nrc_outage_reports, 95/95 unit-name reconciliation); the outage-adjacent SIGNAL hypothesis (unplanned power drops vs. operator returns) stays gate-2-locked — RAW display only, no predictive claim.

layers.name: FAA airport status (ground stops / delays / closures)
layers.source: FAA National Airspace System Status (nasstatus.faa.gov, public domain, keyless)
layers.description: Ground stops, ground-delay programs, arrival/departure delays, and closures as currently published by the FAA — a rolling SNAPSHOT, not an event log (no published end-to-end durations; this session's own capture time is the only lower bound on how long an event has been active). Position comes from a curated client-side table of major US commercial + cargo-hub airports (client/src/lib/faaAirports.ts) since the feed itself reports only a 3-letter ARPT code, no coordinates — an event at an airport outside that table is honestly omitted from the map, never guessed, and the count is disclosed in the layer's status line. Marker color is the event TYPE the feed itself reports (ground stop / closure / ground-delay program / arrival-departure delay), never a graded severity inferred from the free-text avg/max delay strings. RAW, no predictive claim; not for safety-of-life use.

layers.name: CBP land-border wait times
layers.source: CBP Border Wait Times (bwt.cbp.gov, public domain, keyless)
layers.description: Hourly commercial and passenger vehicle wait times at all 84 US land ports of entry the CBP feed currently reports (Canadian + Mexican borders), flattened per lane class (commercial standard / commercial FAST / passenger standard). Position comes from a curated client-side coordinate table (client/src/lib/cbpBorderCrossings.ts) verified per-crossing against independent public sources — a port_number outside that table is honestly omitted, never guessed. Marker color is the worst (max) currently published delay across a port's lanes — a RAW numeric field the feed itself reports, never a derived signal; a lane with no published reading shows as no-data, never coerced to zero. RAW, no predictive claim; fills the ROAD leg of the freight-proxy set (sea=AIS, rail=STB, air=ADS-B).

layers.name: Nuclear facilities (fuel cycle)
layers.source: Wikidata (CC0 1.0), curated through a quality gate
layers.description: 67 nuclear fuel-cycle and production facilities worldwide (Hanford, Sellafield, Mayak, Savannah River, La Hague, Y-12, Los Alamos, Pantex…): uranium enrichment plants, reprocessing sites, radioactive-waste repositories, nuclear test-site facilities (the site entities — individual detonations live in the Nuclear Tests layer) and weapons-complex sites, building-trefoil symbols colored by category. Power plants and reactors EXCLUDED — the two power-plant layers cover them. Curation gate: English label + valid coordinates required, power-plant-classed items dropped, 4 US weapons-complex sites resolved individually. Locations as catalogued (Wikidata qid provenance per marker); no activity, output, or risk claims.

layers.name: Military installations
layers.source: US DoD open data, OpenStreetMap contributors (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), and cited government publications
layers.description: Officially published installation locations. Sources: US DoD open data, OpenStreetMap contributors, and cited government publications. Reference geography only — current as of retrieval date; not operational information. Installation-level only (name, boundary/centroid, branch, type); ~3,024 named installations from OpenStreetMap military=base (US bases included) plus any cited government publications. STATIC REFERENCE GEOGRAPHY: never joined to live aircraft/vessel tracking or any correlation feature (noCrossTies). Default OFF (heavy). Colour by operator nation — muted reference palette, not a threat board.

provenance.license: OpenStreetMap ODbL (attribution required); US DoD open data (public domain); cited government publications
provenance.coverage: global — named military=base installations (installation-level); US DoD authoritative overlay pending

layers.name: Superfund sites (EPA NPL)
layers.source: U.S. EPA Superfund National Priorities List (NPL), SEMS — public domain
layers.description: EPA National Priorities List Superfund sites (~1,840): the nation's most contaminated cleanup sites, colored by NPL status (active / proposed / deleted). Click a site for its status, Hazard Ranking System (HRS) score, location, and listing date. FACTUAL records — location/status/score as EPA publishes them, NOT a risk claim about any specific property (that would be a ladder-gated signal). Every site passes the data-quality gate at ingest (valid coordinates, name, known status, HRS 0–100); failures are quarantined. Refreshed server-side weekly. First layer of the location context engine.

layers.name: Nuclear tests 1945–1998 (time machine)
layers.source: SIPRI / Johnston archive nuclear explosions catalog (public factual data)
layers.description: SIPRI / Johnston archive nuclear explosions catalog 1945-1998 (2,027 located tests): emplacement SYMBOLS (airburst / surface-tower / water / underground shaft) tinted by testing state, yield-scaled; click any test for the decoded catalog record — who ran it, how it was fired, the catalog's stated purpose, and yield in Hiroshima-scale terms. Rings are 5-psi severe-blast-radius ESTIMATES (Glasstone & Dolan cube-root scaling from catalogued yield; buried shots contained, no ring) — labeled estimates, NEVER fallout modeling. Drag the year bar to travel; the selected year pulses. FACTUAL records as catalogued.

layers.name: Earthquakes 1900–now (time machine)
layers.source: USGS ANSS Comprehensive Catalog (ComCat), public domain
layers.description: Every catalogued M6.0+ earthquake since 1900 (14,492 events, compiled through the data-quality gate — 0 quarantined). Shares the history time bar with the nuclear-tests layer: drag through the decades, quakes accumulate, the selected year's events pulse; size and color scale with magnitude (1960 Valdivia M9.5 is the biggest). Click a quake for magnitude, date, depth, place. Historical snapshot to the compile date — the LIVE earthquakes layer covers the present.

layers.name: Water violators (EPA CWA)
layers.source: U.S. EPA ECHO — Clean Water Act compliance records (public domain)
layers.description: Active facilities with MORE THAN 8 of the last 12 quarters in Clean Water Act noncompliance (~25k), from EPA's own enforcement records. Colored by violation kind: red = effluent (actual discharge) violations, amber = failure to report, violet = schedule violations. Click a facility for its permit, quarters in violation, and enforcement-action count. FACTS about permits and violations as EPA publishes them — NOT a water-safety claim about any location (that would be a ladder-gated signal). Data-quality gated at ingest; weekly server-side refresh.

layers.name: PFAS drinking-water detections (EPA UCMR 5)
layers.source: U.S. EPA Fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR 5), public domain — service-area location: EPA Community Water System Service Areas
layers.description: 3,417 public water systems with at least one detected PFAS ('forever chemical') compound in EPA's UCMR 5 national monitoring (2023-2025 cycle, 29 analytes tested, 37,546 detection records). Droplet-with-chemical-ring symbols tinted by the COUNT of distinct PFAS compounds detected (1 / 2-3 / 4+) — a factual count, NOT a concentration or health-risk tier. Click a system for its detected compounds, max reported concentration, and detection dates. Location is the system's service-area boundary CENTROID (an approximation, stated as such), not the exact intake. FACTS as EPA publishes them — NOT an MCL-exceedance or health-risk claim: PFAS MCL compliance monitoring under the 2024 NPDWR doesn't begin until 2027-2029, and UCMR5 predates that compliance data. Rebuilt session-side (scripts/pfas_ucmr5.py) on EPA's own release cadence (roughly quarterly), not a live poll.

layers.name: County cancer rates (NCI State Cancer Profiles)
layers.source: National Cancer Institute, State Cancer Profiles (statecancerprofiles.cancer.gov) — SEER+NPCR county of residence data, public domain
layers.description: Age-adjusted cancer incidence and mortality rates (cases/deaths per 100,000, All Cancer Sites combined, 2018-2022) for 3,143 US counties, choropleth-filled by incidence rate. COUNTY-LEVEL AGGREGATE STATISTIC ONLY — describes the whole county's reported population, never a specific address or resident (ecological fallacy guard); displayed at the county polygon, never as a point. Counties with no NCI record (Puerto Rico, a handful of boundary edge cases) render as 'no data', not a false zero. Suppressed cells (fewer than 16 reported records) show as null, not zero. Click a county for its incidence and mortality rate, trend, and confidence interval. GATE 1 cross-checked at build time against CDC's own separately-published national headline figures (scripts/cdc_cancer_rates.py). Rebuilt session-side on NCI's own multi-year publication cadence, not a live poll.

layers.name: Ambient radiation (gamma)
layers.source: BfS ODL Germany (DL-DE-BY-2.0) · Health Canada FPSN (OGL-Canada) · STUK/FMI Finland (CC BY 4.0) · EPA RadNet US (public domain)
layers.description: Observed ambient gamma dose-rate monitors from four national networks (~2,070 stations: DE 1,681 · CA 66 · FI 248 · US ~76), trefoil symbols tinted by dose display-band. Readings displayed exactly as each network publishes them — no interpolation, no modeling, no health claims. US RadNet monitors draw as TRANSLUCENT CIRCLES spanning roughly each city's land area (EPA publishes city names only — the instrument is somewhere within the circle; radius = the city's Census land area as an equivalent circle); monitors that publish only count rates show CPM, never converted to dose. 3h server refresh. EURDEP deliberately excluded (license requires provider permission).

layers.name: Nuclear accidents & incidents
layers.source: Wikidata (CC0 1.0), curated through a quality gate
layers.description: 46 nuclear and radiological accident/incident sites 1949-2024 (Chernobyl, Fukushima, Kyshtym, Three Mile Island, Windscale, SL-1, Goiânia, Church Rock…), hazard-triangle-trefoil symbols tinted by the official INES severity level where Wikidata catalogs one (P2127) — levels are NEVER inferred, unrated events render gray and say so. Distinct symbol from nuclear TESTS (deliberate detonations) per the symbols directive. Curation gate: English label + date-or-INES evidence required, same-site/date duplicates merged keeping highest INES, three majors resolved individually; each marker links its Wikidata provenance (qid). Static history, refreshed by session curation.

layers.name: FEMA flood hazard zones
layers.source: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL), public domain — tiles rendered live by FEMA's own public map service
layers.description: FEMA's official flood zone map: Special Flood Hazard Areas (1% annual-chance flood, coastal velocity zones) and moderate/minimal-risk zones, colored per FEMA's own legend. Rendered live from FEMA's public service (hazards.fema.gov) — zero server cost, no data archived by us for the overlay. Only visible at property-level zoom (FEMA's own scale limit; renders blank when zoomed out). The location dossier's click-anywhere card separately reports the FEMA-published zone code, Special Flood Hazard Area status, and base flood elevation AT the clicked point — a fact about the zone designation, never a property risk claim (that would be a ladder-gated signal). Areas outside NFHL's mapped footprint are reported honestly as unmapped, never shown as low-risk.

This MASTER toggle shows the entire US grid at once; per-state toggles under 'Power grid — by state' control each individually. As-is display: today's ranked panel + a market-wide seed-total trend + a per-ticker archive lookup; attention-spikes-lead-volume is an open gate-2 hypothesis, gated on trailing archive depth, not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: Commitments of Traders (CFTC, disaggregated)
layers.source: CFTC Public Reporting Socrata API, disaggregated futures-only (no API key required)
layers.description: Weekly futures-only positioning by trader category (producer/merchant, swap dealer, managed money, other reportables), ~274 markets. As-is display: a market search + per-market managed-money net-position history + today's ranked panel by |net % of open interest|; positioning-extremes-mean-revert is an open gate-2 hypothesis, gated on trailing archive depth, not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: Traders in Financial Futures (CFTC, futures-only)
layers.source: CFTC Public Reporting Socrata API, futures-only (no API key required, keyless sibling of the disaggregated COT stream)
layers.description: Weekly financial-futures positioning by trader category (dealer/intermediary, asset manager, leveraged money, other reportables) — ES/NQ/rates/FX-class markets. As-is display: today's ranked panel by |leveraged-money net % of open interest|, with dealer net shown alongside. Leveraged-money-extremes-mean-revert (dealer as the informed side) is an open gate-2 hypothesis, gated on trailing archive depth (no /history endpoint yet), not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: US Treasury auctions
layers.source: TreasuryDirect TA_WS, securities/auctioned (US government work, public domain, no API key required)
layers.description: Primary-market results for Bill/Note/Bond/TIPS/FRN/CMB auctions from the last 30 days: bid-to-cover, high yield/discount rate, and dealer/direct/indirect bidder-class shares (dealer_take published by the route, direct/indirect take derived client-side from the same competitive-accepted denominator). Bid-to-cover-deterioration-and-rising-dealer-take-precede-rate-regime-shifts is an open gate-2 hypothesis, not yet surfaced as a signal; the classic tail-vs-when-issued stress metric needs a 1pm ET WI quote, which is paid data and is never faked here.

layers.name: Treasury Daily Statement
layers.source: U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data API, deposits_withdrawals_operating_cash (US government work, public domain, no API key required)
layers.description: Most recent published Daily Treasury Statement: all operating-cash deposit/withdrawal line items by category and account, $ millions as published (~1-2 business-day lag). Withheld-tax-deposits-form-a-daily-payroll-nowcast-weeks-ahead-of-BLS-releases (plus corporate-tax/FUTA deltas nowcasting macro turns) is an open gate-1 hypothesis, not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: FDA binary events
layers.source: openFDA drugsfda API + Federal Register API (both US government work, public domain, no API key required)
layers.description: openFDA approvals from the last 30 days (backward-looking confirmations) plus Federal Register FDA advisory-committee meeting notices (forward-looking catalysts; meeting date parsed from the notice text where stated, labeled 'unparsed' rather than guessed otherwise). No PDUFA target dates — legally unavailable free (21 CFR 314.430). Binary-event-timing-drives-biotech-options-IV-into-scheduled-catalysts (a theta-side input, not directional) is an open gate-2 hypothesis, not yet attempted, not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: Vehicle complaints
layers.source: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation complaints API (US government work, public domain, no API key required)
layers.description: Per-vehicle complaint counts (total, crash-flagged, fire-flagged) over a curated ticker-mapped make/model/year watchlist — not the full NHTSA vehicle universe; an unlisted make/model was never polled, not screened out. Complaint-rate-acceleration-precedes-recalls-and-investigations (especially crash/fire flags) is an open gate-1 hypothesis, not yet attempted, not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: Bank failures
layers.source: FDIC Bank Data API — bank failures (US government data, keyless, no API key required)
layers.description: Most recent US bank failure and assistance events (name, state, type, assets/deposits, estimated DIF cost) back to 1934; v1 scope is failures only, not the quarterly financials snapshot. No ticker join — most failed institutions are small, non-public regional banks. Deposit-flight-and-failures-at-small-regional-banks-lead-KRE-and-listed-small-cap-banks is an open gate-1 hypothesis, not yet attempted, not yet surfaced as a signal.

layers.name: Dark-ship statistics
layers.source: Derived from our own AIS archive (terrestrial coverage)
layers.description: Event COUNTS from our own vessel archive: AIS gap events (silent >6h, reappeared >100km away), identity-change candidates, loitering in known STS/transshipment zones. A gap can be coverage loss, not dark sailing — per-vessel shadow-fleet claims are SIGNAL-class and stay gated until validated (ladder gate 1).

layers.name: Port dwell (arrivals/departures)
layers.source: Derived from our own AIS archive + imagery-verified port geofences
layers.description: Per-port vessel dwell statistics from our own archive: completed calls, ships in port now, median/p90 dwell, and 3x-median anomaly FLAGS (suppressed under 10 completed calls — thin history). Dwell figures are lower bounds (coverage gaps split visits). The dwell-anomaly SIGNAL (congestion predicts returns) stays gated at ladder gate 2 vs published congestion indices.

layers.name: Everything Graph
layers.source: Own join over SEC EDGAR Form 4 + datacore/entity_map.json + own AIS-derived port-dwell archive (datacore/EVERYTHING_GRAPH.md)
layers.description: Search a ticker, insider CIK, vessel MMSI, or facility id to see everything the platform has joined about it: insiders, operated facilities, vessels calling at its ports. RAW join with provenance on every edge (source, confidence, first/last seen) — no predictive claim; any future anomaly/interpretation layer on top is SIGNAL-class and ladder-gated separately.

layers.name: Active fires (VIIRS)
layers.source: NASA FIRMS / LANCE (VIIRS 375m NRT; free MAP_KEY)
layers.description: Active-fire detections, ~3h latency. Not for safety-of-life use. Goes live automatically when NASA_FIRMS_MAP_KEY is set (free registration — see wishlist). No free history exists upstream — detections archive from the day the key activates.

layers.name: Night lights radiance (GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — VIIRS/SNPP Day/Night Band, public domain
layers.description: Daily night-lights radiance imagery, dated (default: yesterday — GIBS never carries same-day data; step back further via the on-panel scrubber). As-is display, no predictive claim — metro/industrial radiance MoM/YoY delta as a regional-economic-activity proxy is an open gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet surfaced as a signal. Some dates/areas render blank on the daylight side of the terminator or from sensor gaps — honest, not a bug.

layers.name: Aerosol optical depth (GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — MODIS Combined Value-Added AOD (Terra+Aqua), public domain
layers.description: Daily aerosol optical depth — how much haze, smoke, and dust the atmosphere holds — dated (default: yesterday; step back via the on-panel scrubber). As-is display, no predictive claim: AOD over an industrial basin or shipping lane as an output/PMI proxy (dry-bulk, air-freight, China-export) is an open gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet a signal. Gaps over cloud/glint/high-albedo areas render blank — the retrieval's honest coverage, not a bug.

layers.name: Vegetation health (NDVI, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — VIIRS/SNPP NDVI 8-day composite, public domain
layers.description: Vegetation greenness (NDVI) as an 8-day composite — greener = denser/healthier canopy — dated (default: yesterday returns the current composite; step back via the on-panel scrubber). As-is display, no predictive claim: an NDVI anomaly over a named crop belt as a yield proxy (CBOT corn/soy/wheat) is an open gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet a signal. Ocean and barren areas are legitimately blank — NDVI is a land-vegetation index, not a bug.

layers.name: Soil moisture (SMAP, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture, public domain
layers.description: Root-zone soil moisture from NASA SMAP L4, dated. NOTE the ~6-day processing lag: the scrubber defaults ~7 days back (not yesterday) because SMAP L4 does not carry recent days — defaulting to yesterday would show a guaranteed-blank tile. As-is display, no predictive claim: soil moisture over a named crop belt (with drought/river layers) as an agricultural-supply proxy is an open gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet a signal. Ocean is legitimately blank — this is a land soil index.

layers.name: Nitrogen dioxide (TROPOMI, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI tropospheric NO₂ column, public domain
layers.description: Tropospheric nitrogen-dioxide column density (daily, from ESA Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI via NASA GIBS), dated (default: yesterday; step back via the on-panel scrubber). NO₂ is a short-lived combustion by-product, so the field tracks active industry and traffic. As-is display, no predictive claim: NO₂ over an industrial zone/port as a real-time throughput nowcast (leads PMI/industrial-production) is an open gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet a signal. Satellite-swath gaps and cloud cover leave stripes/blanks — honest coverage, not a bug.

layers.name: Sulfur dioxide, planetary boundary layer (OMPS, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — Suomi NPP/NOAA-20 OMPS sulfur-dioxide column (planetary boundary layer), public domain
layers.description: Sulfur-dioxide column density in the planetary boundary layer (nearest-surface of GIBS's three SO₂ altitude bands), dated (default: yesterday; step back via the on-panel scrubber). As-is display, no predictive claim: SO₂ over a named volcano (vs. the volcanoes layer's USGS elevated-alert levels, shipped 2026-08-02) as a degassing signal, and SO₂ over a named smelter/refinery/coal plant (vs. powerplants and coal_mine_features) as an activity proxy, are both open gate-2 hypotheses (research/open_questions.md), not yet signals. Satellite-swath gaps and cloud cover leave stripes/blanks — honest coverage, not a bug.

layers.name: Flood / water extent (MODIS, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — MODIS Terra+Aqua 3-day combined flood composite, public domain
layers.description: Rolling 3-day surface-water/flood extent composite from MODIS Terra+Aqua, dated (default: yesterday; step back via the on-panel scrubber). Shows ALL standing water — normal rivers, lakes, and reservoirs as well as flood anomalies — this is the honest reading of a water-extent composite, not a defect (distinct from the separate floodzones layer, FEMA's static regulatory hazard-zone designation — this layer is observed current water, not designated risk). As-is display, no predictive claim: flooding over industrial parks/ports/farmland as an exposure signal for insurers, auto/semiconductor plants, and acreage loss is an open gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet a signal. Cloud cover can leave gaps.

layers.name: Aboveground biomass density (GEDI, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — GEDI L4B aboveground biomass density, mission-life mean, public domain
layers.description: Aboveground biomass density from NASA's GEDI spaceborne LiDAR (ISS), a single static composite averaged over the mission's 2019-04 through 2023-03 record — not a daily/dated product like the other GIBS layers here, so there is no time scrubber. As-is display, no predictive claim: standing forest carbon stock as a substrate for a future carbon/timber/land-use gate-2 hypothesis (research/open_questions.md), not yet a signal. GEDI is limited to roughly ±51.6° latitude and land vegetation only, so poles, oceans, and non-forested land are legitimately blank — the honest coverage boundary of a spaceborne LiDAR product, not a gap.

layers.name: Fire/hotspot temperature (GOES-East, GIBS)
layers.source: NASA GIBS/ESDIS — GOES-East ABI fire/hotspot brightness temperature (v0 NRT), public domain
layers.description: Continuous full-disk brightness-temperature field from the GOES-East weather satellite, ~10-minute cadence with irregular scan gaps (not a fixed daily schedule like the other GIBS layers on this map — always shows the most recent available scan, no date scrubber). Brighter/hotter pixels indicate fire and other thermal anomalies. Coverage is GOES-East's fixed Americas + Atlantic scan domain, not global — blank tiles outside that domain are the honest edge, not an error. This complements, and does not replace, the NASA FIRMS active-fire point-detection layer above: FIRMS gives discrete confirmed detections at ~3h latency; this gives a continuous heat-intensity field at ~10-min cadence. Not for safety-of-life use. As-is display, no predictive claim — the fires × facility-exposure hypothesis (research/open_questions.md) is already filed against the FIRMS layer and is unchanged by this addition.

layers.name: Methane plumes (GEM GMET)
layers.source: Global Energy Monitor — Methane Emitters Tracker (GMET), CarbonMapper/GHGSat-class satellite detections, CC BY 4.0
layers.description: 3,473 dated satellite methane-plume detections, each shown with the nearest catalogued GEM oil/gas-extraction or coal-mine asset within 2km (server/gemMethaneProximity.ts) — a geometric proximity fact, not a claimed emissions attribution. As-is display, no predictive claim: the plume×extraction-registry proximity hypothesis (research/open_questions.md) is gate-2(a) only — repeat-detection rate, a same-universe base rate, and matching against operators' own disclosed emissions are still unbuilt. Detections with nothing catalogued within 2km render as unmatched, honestly, rather than guessed.

layers.name: Coal mine boundaries & infrastructure (GEM)
layers.source: Global Energy Monitor — Coal Mine Boundaries and Methane Sources, CC BY 4.0 (server/gemCoalMineFeatures.ts)
layers.description: 2,116 catalogued mine features: 333 mine-boundary polygons plus 1,783 point features — ventilation shafts, degasification/drainage wells, and other mapped mine infrastructure (preparation plants, coal storage, combined heat and power). This is the underlying GEM asset geometry the Methane Plumes layer above already matches detections against, shown directly for the first time. Symbol = feature category (boundary / ventilation / degasification / other); colour = catalogued coal grade (metallurgical / thermal / thermal & met / unstated) — never a production or output claim. Locations and boundaries as catalogued by GEM; no activity, output, or emissions claims. Off by default (same GEM-family precedent as Methane Plumes).

layers.name: River gauges (barge corridor)
layers.source: USGS NWIS (public domain)
layers.description: Live stage/discharge at 14 Mississippi/Ohio barge-corridor gauges. Raw readings as published (provisional values revise); the low-water freight-stress signal is gate-2-locked.

layers.name: Severe weather alerts (NWS)
layers.source: National Weather Service (public domain)
layers.description: Active NWS warnings/watches with polygons, colored by severity, ~10-min refresh. Official alerts displayed as-is; zone-coded alerts without polygons are counted, not drawn (follow-up filed). Not for safety-of-life use.

layers.name: Space weather (NOAA SWPC)
layers.source: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (public domain)
layers.description: Aurora oval (OVATION Prime MODEL FORECAST, labeled as forecast) + observed planetary Kp, R/S/G storm scales, solar-wind summary, and GOES X-ray flare class (NOAA's own A/B/C/M/X formula), ~10-min refresh. Observed vs forecast carried per row, never blended; the grid/utility hypothesis is validation-gated.

layers.name: Large meteors (NASA)
layers.description: Big meteors that exploded in the atmosphere (bolides), detected by US Government sensors and published by NASA/JPL CNEOS after the fact — a few dozen per year worldwide. Symbol = blast; color = blast energy (kt TNT); streak = direction of travel, drawn only for events where NASA publishes the velocity vector. Events accumulate in our archive; ~6h refresh.
layers.source: NASA/JPL CNEOS fireball API (US Government sensors) — public domain, self-archived

layers.name: Earthquakes (USGS)
layers.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (public domain)
layers.description: Real-time M2.5+ seismic events worldwide, rolling 24h window, sized and colored by magnitude. Official USGS feed displayed as-is; not for safety-of-life use.

layers.name: Volcano alert levels (USGS/GVP)
layers.source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program (elevated alert levels, public domain) + Global Volcanism Program, Smithsonian Institution (volcano coordinates, Volcanoes of the World database — a US-federal-employee-authored compilation per GVP's own citation policy, not the site's general non-commercial narrative/photo Content)
layers.description: Currently-elevated volcanoes worldwide (USGS Volcano Hazards Program alert level: ADVISORY/WATCH/WARNING, color-coded YELLOW/ORANGE/RED), coordinates joined live per-request from GVP's public WFS database rather than a static reference table (rescoped 2026-08-01 from an assumed static join; the live join needs no stale-data maintenance). As-is display, no predictive claim. A vnum with no GVP coordinate match still counts but cannot be placed on the map (rare; USGS's Volcano Numbers are the same scheme GVP catalogs). Cross-ties (open_questions.md, gate-2 hypotheses, not claimed here): volcanic degassing vs. the SO2 layer, aviation ash risk vs. aircraft, and nearby USGS earthquake activity.

layers.name: Ocean buoys (NDBC)
layers.source: NOAA National Data Buoy Center (public domain)
layers.description: Latest wave height, period, and pressure readings from ~889 NDBC/C-MAN stations worldwide. Raw observations as published; missing sensors reported as no-data, never zero.

layers.name: Surface water (1984–2021)
layers.source: EC JRC/Google — Global Surface Water v2021 (Pekel et al. 2016; free with attribution)
layers.description: Where surface water occurred over 1984–2021 (occurrence % — rare to permanent). STATIC dataset, not live conditions: v2021 vintage stated per the imagery-date honesty rule. Atlas-parity layer; tiles served directly from the JRC public bucket — zero server cost.

layers.name: Forest cover (2020)
layers.source: EC JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 (10m, CC BY 4.0) — tiles via Global Forest Watch
layers.description: Where forest stood in 2020 at 10m resolution. STATIC dataset, not live conditions: 2020 vintage stated per the imagery-date honesty rule. Atlas-parity layer; tiles served directly from the GFW public tile API — zero server cost.

layers.name: Country borders
layers.source: Natural Earth 1:110m admin-0 (public domain) — compiled into datacore
layers.description: Country boundary lines as a reference overlay. Generalized 1:110m coastlines/borders (not survey-grade); de-facto boundaries per Natural Earth policy. Self-hosted — zero external dependency.

layers.name: Time zone lines
layers.description: Where clocks change: borders between land time zones (solid) and the International Date Line / ocean nautical-zone meridians (dashed). Compiled from timezone-boundary-builder 2025b (ODbL), zones merged where rules are identical TODAY and simplified for display — lines are approximate near borders, not survey-grade. Static client asset — zero server cost.
layers.source: timezone-boundary-builder 2025b (ODbL) — innerlines compile, self-hosted

layers.name: State / province borders
layers.source: Natural Earth 1:50m admin-1 (public domain) — compiled into datacore
layers.description: State and province boundary lines (first-level subdivisions, worldwide) as a thin reference overlay. Generalized 1:50m (not survey-grade); de-facto boundaries per Natural Earth policy. Fades in around zoom 3. Self-hosted — zero external dependency.

layers.name: Celestial paths
layers.source: astronomy-engine ephemeris (computed, MIT) — no feed
layers.description: Ecliptic and Moon/planet sky tracks drawn on the always-on celestial sky, from real ephemeris in a frozen sidereal frame; segments below the horizon fade out. Reference lines, not observations. Computed on-device — zero network cost.

layers.name: Places & labels
layers.source: GeoNames gazetteer (CC BY 4.0) — compiled to vector tiles by our pipeline
layers.description: Named places across the whole world — countries, states/provinces, cities & towns, ISLANDS, seas & bays — as our own vector-tile labels layer (built from GeoNames, CC BY, storeable/ownable unlike Google's). Zoom-tiered so the map reads at every scale; tap a label to see what a place is. On by default for discovery. Photorealistic 3D imagery of a place is the separate Google 3D Tiles path at deep zoom.

layers.name: Tank-fill % (Sentinel-2)
layers.source: Copernicus Sentinel-2 shadow analysis
layers.description: GATED: may not surface before ladder gate 2 (statistical validation vs EIA ground truth).
